title: The far-infrared/radio correlation for a sample of strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies detected by Herschel
question: Investigate the radio-far infrared (FIR) correlation, its redshift evolution, and its radio luminosity dependence for a sample of 28 strongly lensed high-redshift dusty star-forming galaxies.

data.angular_resolution: ~1.7 arcsec (SGP Band 4), ~1.2 to <0.1 arcsec (Northern and Equatorial Bands 4, 6, 7)

what.value: Parent catalog of 80 candidate strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies with S_500um > 100 mJy and redshifts

evidence.quote: (cite: Negrello2017) extracted a sample of 80 bright FIR/submm-selected galaxies with flux density $S_{500\mu\rm m}>100\,$mJy from the H-ATLAS fields.

what.value: H-ATLAS Data Release 1 and 2 point-source Herschel/SPIRE photometry

evidence.quote: The SPIRE photometry is obtained from the point-source Herschel/SPIRE catalogues of the H-ATLAS Data Release 1 and 2, described in (cite: Valiante2016) and (cite: Maddox2017a).

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts of H-ATLASJ130333.1+244643, H-ATLASJ131540.6+262322 and H-ATLASJ133255.7+342207

evidence.quote: $^\dag$ spectroscopic redshifts of H-ATLASJ130333.1+244643, H-ATLASJ131540.6+262322 and H-ATLASJ133255.7+342207 are taken from (cite: Neri2020).

what.value: JVLA 7 GHz radio flux density converted to 1.4 GHz for H-ATLAS J142935.3-002836

evidence.quote: For one of the matched source, namely H-ATLAS J142935.3-002836, the FIRST flux density value has been replaced with the more reliable one coming from the JVLA 7 GHz high resolution ($\sim$ 0.3 arcsec) and high sensitivity (10 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$) observations described in (cite: Messias2014) (converted at 1.4 GHz).

what.value: JVLA 6.89 GHz radio flux density reported at 1.4 GHz for H-ATLASJ133542.9+300401

evidence.quote: Observations at 6.89 GHz from the JVLA are available for one additional source (H-ATLASJ133542.9+300401) and are described in details by (cite: Nayyeri2017).

what.value: Comparison sample of strongly gravitationally-lensed quasars with FIR and radio measurements

evidence.loc: The FIR-radio correlation for (candidate) lensed galaxies
evidence.quote: Such a behaviour is similar to what have been revealed by (cite: Stacey2018) observing a sample of strong gravitationally-lensed quasars.

evidence.loc: The FIR-radio correlation for (candidate) lensed galaxies
evidence.quote: Two additional sources are the gravitationally lensed radio-quiet quasars targeted by the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) and detected by Herschel described in (cite: Stacey2019).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and extract 2.1 GHz radio continuum flux densities from ATCA observations
recipe.method: Automatic flagging with PGFLAG, standard 16 cm calibration, uv-combination with UVAVER, self-calibration, Briggs-weighted (robust=0.5) continuum imaging in Miriad, and conversion from 2.1 GHz to 1.4 GHz using a power-law spectral index
key_parameters: 5% calibration error added in quadrature to image noise
assumptions: Power-law radio spectrum S_nu = nu^alpha with alpha = -0.7 +/- 0.14

recipe.goal: Cross-match H-ATLAS candidates with FIRST, ATCA, and literature radio data using NIR and archival ALMA high-resolution imaging
recipe.method: Cross-match within 10 arcsec of H-ATLAS position in FIRST catalogue/maps and ATCA maps for >3 sigma detections, selecting the component nearest to the SPIRE peak that overlaps with NIR (HST, UKIDSS, VIKING) or archival ALMA Band 4/6/7 continuum emission
key_parameters: Detection threshold > 3 sigma (and 3 sigma upper limits for non-detections)
assumptions: Observed SPIRE flux density is mostly originated by the lensed object with negligible contamination from nearby sources in the Herschel beam

recipe.goal: Compute rest-frame 1.4 GHz radio luminosities, integrated FIR luminosities (8-1000 um), and q_FIR parameters
recipe.method: Compute L_1.4GHz from 1.4 GHz flux densities, fit Herschel/SPIRE photometry with an optically-thin single-temperature modified blackbody integrated from 8 to 1000 um to obtain L_FIR, and calculate q_FIR (all uncorrected for lensing magnification)
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with Omega_M = 0.32, Omega_Lambda = 0.63, Omega_b = 0.05, h = 0.67, sigma_8 = 0.81
Optically-thin single-temperature modified blackbody with dust emissivity index beta = 1.5

answer_key.quantity: Number of candidate lensed galaxies with detected radio counterparts

evidence.quote: Therefore, combining ATCA follow-up and FIRST cross-matches we collected radio measurements for 28 out of the 80 galaxies in the original sample by (cite: Negrello2017), that will constitute our reference in the present paper.

answer_key.quantity: Median rest-frame 1.4 GHz radio luminosity L_1.4GHz (uncorrected for magnification)

evidence.quote: Our 28 objects span a range $1.9\times10^{24}\lesssim L_{\rm 1.4 GHz}\lesssim 1.8\times 10^{26}$ W Hz$^{-1}$ (uncorrected for the lens magnification factor $\mu$), with a median value of $L_{\rm 1.4 GHz}\sim 2.4\times 10^{25}$ W Hz$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Median FIR luminosity L_FIR (uncorrected for magnification)

evidence.quote: The FIR luminosities span the range $1.3\times 10^{13}\lesssim L_{\rm FIR} \lesssim 1.1\times 10^{14}$ $L_{\odot}$, with a median value of $L_{\rm FIR} \sim 3.5 \times 10^{13}$ $L_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Median dust temperature T_dust for the total sample of candidate strongly lensed galaxies

evidence.quote: The median value of the dust temperature for the total sample of candidate strongly lensed galaxies is $T_{\rm dust}= 35.2 \pm 2.1$, consistently with what was found by (cite: Negrello2017) for the same sample.
